pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts all three seeded items are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
src/index.js item() prefixes '★ ' only when starred; 'AC-2' test checks the exact list with one starred item.
'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and expects ['★ First item','★ Third item'], so order is by id, with status 200.
'AC-4' checks both / and /?show=all give all three items in id order; the query still ends in ORDER BY id.
'AC-5' checks the exact 'Starred only' link on / and the 'All items' link on the starred view.
Object.hasOwn guard returns 400; 'AC-6' covers Starred, none, empty and __proto__, and checks the body has no <li>.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'; 'AC-7' asserts it. traffic/src/index.js passes the routes through unchanged.

lenses.note: Change matches the spec's intent and both decisions: order unchanged, and the view is a GET query parameter. Nothing beyond the ask. The traffic-check regex relaxation is needed for AC-7 and is disclosed in the PR.
All 7 AC items and all 4 state rows are implemented and named by tests. The spec is added in this change with a go dated 2026-10-12, and no later commit edits an acceptance item.

Tests assert rendered items, status and messages, and each state row has its own test. The DB is reset before every test by test/apply-migrations.js. I could not run npm test here because vitest is not installed; CI covers it. The traffic fake and traffic-config.test.sh are extended without being loosened, and fragment and space rejections are newly tested.
README describes ?show=starred. The migration and the routes file are self-explanatory.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ is safe. The SQL is built only from fixed VIEWS strings, never from user input. An empty show= gives 400, as specified.
The query parameter is only used as a lookup key, never interpolated. Titles are still HTML-escaped. No instructions were planted in the repository content.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework, styles or browser flow. I judged this a non-UI change.
